definitions.explanation: The ability to sense or understand others' feelings, situations, or unspoken intentions without being told directly. A key concept in Japanese interpersonal communication.

examples.japanese: {察|さっ}し⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{悪|わる}くて→悪い：00908_warui⟧、⟦{相手|あいて}→相手：01677_aite⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{気持|きも}ち⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{気|き}づけなかった。
examples.english: I was insensitive and couldn't notice the other person's feelings.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{言葉|ことば}→言葉：02880_kotoba⟧にしなくて⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{察|さっ}し⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{通|つう}じる→通じる：02289_tsuujiru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: In Japan, things are often communicated through unspoken understanding rather than words.

notes:
{察|さっ}し is the noun form of ⟦{察|さっ}する→察する：08053_sassuru⟧ (to sense, to perceive). It describes the ability to read between the lines and understand what is not explicitly stated.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {察|さっ}し⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧ (perceptive, quick to pick up on things)
- {察|さっ}し⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{悪|わる}い→悪い：00908_warui⟧ (insensitive, slow to pick up on things)
- {察|さっ}し⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧つく (to be able to guess/sense)
- お{察|さっ}し⟦します→する：00392_suru⟧ (I can imagine how you feel — polite expression of empathy)

CULTURAL NOTE:
{察|さっ}し is considered a core aspect of Japanese communication style. Japanese culture places high value on being able to understand others' feelings and intentions without explicit verbal expression. Being described as {察|さっ}し⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧ is a significant compliment, while {察|さっ}し⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{悪|わる}い→悪い：00908_warui⟧ can be a pointed criticism.
